text:
The AMD Ryzen 3 8300G is a desktop processor with 4 cores, launched in January 2024, at an MSRP of $176. It is part of the Ryzen 3 lineup, using the Zen 4 (Phoenix) architecture with Socket AM5. Thanks to AMD Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) each core can process two instruction streams in parallel, making better use of available hardware units, for a total of 8 threads. Ryzen 3 8300G has 8 MB of L3 cache and operates at 3.4 GHz by default, but can boost up to 4.9 GHz, depending on the workload. AMD is building the Ryzen 3 8300G on a 4 nm production process using 20.9 billion transistors. The silicon die of the chip is not fabricated at AMD, but at the foundry of TSMC. The multiplier is locked on Ryzen 3 8300G, which limits its overclocking capabilities.
With a TDP of 65 W, the Ryzen 3 8300G consumes typical power levels for a modern PC. AMD's processor supports DDR5 memory with a dual-channel interface. The highest officially supported memory speed is 5200 MT/s, but with overclocking

text:
(and the right memory modules) you can go even higher. ECC memory is supported, too, which is an important capability for mission-critical systems, to avoid data corruption. For communication with other components in the computer, Ryzen 3 8300G uses a PCI-Express Gen 4 connection. This processor features the Radeon 740M integrated graphics solution. Inside the box you will not only find the processor, but also a Wraith Stealth cooler.
Hardware virtualization is available on the Ryzen 3 8300G, which greatly improves virtual machine performance. Programs using Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX) will run on this processor, boosting performance for calculation-heavy applications. Besides AVX, AMD has added support for the newer AVX2 and AVX-512 instructions, too.

text:
The AMD Ryzen 5 8500G is a mobile processor with 6 cores, launched in January 2024, at an MSRP of $179. It is part of the Ryzen 5 lineup, using the Zen 4 (Phoenix) architecture with Socket AM5. Thanks to AMD Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) each core can process two instruction streams in parallel, making better use of available hardware units, for a total of 12 threads. Ryzen 5 8500G has 16 MB of L3 cache and operates at 3.5 GHz by default, but can boost up to 5 GHz, depending on the workload. AMD is making the Ryzen 5 8500G on a 4 nm production node using 20.9 billion transistors. The silicon die of the chip is not fabricated at AMD, but at the foundry of TSMC. The multiplier is locked on Ryzen 5 8500G, which limits its overclocking potential.
With a TDP of 65 W, the Ryzen 5 8500G consumes typical power levels for a modern PC. AMD's processor supports DDR5 memory with a dual-channel interface. The highest officially supported memory speed is 5200 MT/s. ECC memory is supported, too,

which is an important capability for mission-critical systems, to avoid data corruption. For communication with other components in the system, Ryzen 5 8500G uses a PCI-Express Gen 4 connection. This processor features the Radeon 740M integrated graphics solution. Inside the box you will not only find the processor, but also a Wraith Stealth cooler.
Hardware virtualization is available on the Ryzen 5 8500G, which greatly improves virtual machine performance. Programs using Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX) can run on this processor, boosting performance for calculation-heavy applications. text:
The AMD Ryzen 7 7700X is a desktop processor with 8 cores, launched in September 2022, at an MSRP of $399. It is part of the Ryzen 7 lineup, using the Zen 4 (Raphael) architecture with Socket AM5. Thanks to AMD Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) each core can process two instruction streams in parallel, making better use of available hardware units, for a total of 16 threads. Ryzen 7 7700X has 32 MB of L3 cache and operates at 4.5 GHz by default, but can boost up to 5.4 GHz, depending on the workload. AMD is making the Ryzen 7 7700X on a 5 nm production node using 6.57 billion transistors. The silicon die of the chip is not fabricated at AMD, but at the foundry of TSMC. You may freely adjust the unlocked multiplier on Ryzen 7 7700X, which simplifies overclocking greatly, as you can easily dial in any overclocking frequency.
With a TDP of 105 W, the Ryzen 7 7700X consumes a good deal of power, so decent cooling is needed. AMD's processor supports DDR5 memory with a dual-channel interface

metadata.title: AMD Ryzen 7 7700X Specs | TechPowerUp CPU Database

text:
. The highest officially supported memory speed is 5200 MT/s, but with overclocking (and the right memory modules) you can go even higher. ECC memory is supported, too, which is an important capability for mission-critical systems, to avoid data corruption. For communication with other components in the system, Ryzen 7 7700X uses a PCI-Express Gen 5 connection. This processor features the Radeon Graphics integrated graphics solution.
Hardware virtualization is available on the Ryzen 7 7700X, which greatly improves virtual machine performance. Programs using Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX) can run on this processor, boosting performance for calculation-heavy applications. Besides AVX, AMD has added support for the newer AVX2 and AVX-512 instructions, too.

text:
The AMD Ryzen 7 9700X is a desktop processor with 8 cores, launched in August 2024, at an MSRP of $359. It is part of the Ryzen 7 lineup, using the Zen 5 (Granite Ridge) architecture with Socket AM5. Thanks to AMD Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) each core can process two instruction streams in parallel, making better use of available hardware units, for a total of 16 threads. Ryzen 7 9700X has 32 MB of L3 cache and operates at 3.8 GHz by default, but can boost up to 5.5 GHz, depending on the workload. AMD is building the Ryzen 7 9700X on a 4 nm production process using 8.31 billion transistors. The silicon die of the chip is not fabricated at AMD, but at the foundry of TSMC. You may freely adjust the unlocked multiplier on Ryzen 7 9700X, which simplifies overclocking greatly, as you can easily dial in any overclocking frequency.
With a TDP of 65 W, the Ryzen 7 9700X consumes typical power levels for a modern PC. AMD's processor supports DDR5 memory with a dual-channel interface. The

text:
highest officially supported memory speed is 5600 MT/s, but with overclocking (and the right memory modules) you can go even higher. Hardware virtualization is available on the Ryzen 7 9700X, which greatly improves virtual machine performance. text:
The AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D is a desktop processor with 16 cores, launched in January 2023, at an MSRP of $699. It is part of the Ryzen 9 lineup, using the Zen 4 (Raphael) architecture with Socket AM5. Thanks to AMD Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) each core can process two instruction streams in parallel, making better use of available hardware units, for a total of 32 threads. Ryzen 9 7950X3D has 128 MB of L3 cache and operates at 4.2 GHz by default, but can boost up to 5.7 GHz, depending on the workload. AMD is making the Ryzen 9 7950X3D on a 5 nm production node using 17.8 billion transistors. The silicon die of the chip is not fabricated at AMD, but at the foundry of TSMC. You may freely adjust the unlocked multiplier on Ryzen 9 7950X3D, which simplifies overclocking greatly, as you can easily dial in any overclocking frequency.
With a TDP of 120 W, the Ryzen 9 7950X3D consumes a lot of power, so good cooling is definitely needed. AMD's processor supports DDR5 memory with a dual-chan

text:
nel interface. The highest officially supported memory speed is 5200 MT/s, but with overclocking (and the right memory modules) you can go even higher. ECC memory is supported, too, which is an important capability for mission-critical systems, to avoid data corruption. For communication with other components in the computer, Ryzen 9 7950X3D uses a PCI-Express Gen 5 connection. This processor features the Radeon Graphics integrated graphics solution.
Hardware virtualization is available on the Ryzen 9 7950X3D, which greatly improves virtual machine performance. Programs using Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX) can run on this processor, boosting performance for calculation-heavy applications. Besides AVX, AMD has added support for the newer AVX2 and AVX-512 instructions, too.

The AMD Ryzen 9 9950X is a desktop processor with 16 cores, launched in August 2024, at an MSRP of $649. Thanks to AMD Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) each core can process two instruction streams in parallel, making better use of available hardware units, for a total of 32 threads. Ryzen 9 9950X has 64 MB of L3 cache and operates at 4.3 GHz by default, but can boost up to 5.7 GHz, depending on the workload. AMD is building the Ryzen 9 9950X on a 4 nm production process using 16.6 billion transistors. The silicon die of the chip is not fabricated at AMD, but at the foundry of TSMC. You may freely adjust the unlocked multiplier on Ryzen 9 9950X, which simplifies overclocking greatly, as you can easily dial in any overclocking frequency.

hannel interface. The highest officially supported memory speed is 5600 MT/s, but with overclocking (and the right memory modules) you can go even higher. For communication with other components in the system, Ryzen 9 9950X uses a PCI-Express Gen 5 connection. This processor features the Radeon Graphics integrated graphics solution.
Hardware virtualization is available on the Ryzen 9 9950X, which greatly improves virtual machine performance. Programs using Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX) will run on this processor, boosting performance for calculation-heavy applications. Besides AVX, AMD has added support for the newer AVX2 and AVX-512 instructions, too.

metadata.title: AMD Ryzen 9 PRO 9965X3D Specs | TechPowerUp CPU Database

text:
The AMD Ryzen 9 PRO 9965X3D is a server/workstation processor with 16 cores, launched in June 2026. It is part of the Ryzen 9 lineup, using the Zen 5 (Granite Ridge) architecture with Socket AM5. Thanks to AMD Simultaneous Multithreading (SMT) each core can process two instruction streams in parallel, making better use of available hardware units, for a total of 32 threads. Ryzen 9 PRO 9965X3D has 128 MB of L3 cache and operates at 4.3 GHz by default, but can boost up to 5.5 GHz, depending on the workload. AMD is building the Ryzen 9 PRO 9965X3D on a 4 nm production process using 16.6 billion transistors. The silicon die of the chip is not fabricated at AMD, but at the foundry of TSMC. The multiplier is locked on Ryzen 9 PRO 9965X3D, which limits its overclocking capabilities.
With a TDP of 170 W, the Ryzen 9 PRO 9965X3D is extremely power hungry, which means you need top-notch cooling. AMD's processor supports DDR5 memory with a dual-channel interface. The highest officially supported

memory speed is 5600 MT/s. ECC memory is supported, too, which is an important capability for mission-critical systems, to avoid data corruption. For communication with other components in the system, Ryzen 9 PRO 9965X3D uses a PCI-Express Gen 5 connection. This processor features the Radeon Graphics integrated graphics solution.
Hardware virtualization is available on the Ryzen 9 PRO 9965X3D, which greatly improves virtual machine performance. Additionally, IOMMU virtualization (PCI passthrough) is supported, so that guest virtual machines may directly use host hardware. Programs using Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX) will run on this processor, boosting performance for calculation-heavy applications. Besides AVX, AMD has added support for the newer AVX2 and AVX-512 instructions, too.
